target_customer: Small business owners buying Google AdWords keywords without an agency
problem: Small businesses found choosing and bidding on AdWords keywords confusing and costly without an SEM agency.
business_model: SaaS for AdWords management (pricing not found)

founders.name: Antonio Garcia-Martinez
founders.background_notes: Went to Facebook's ads team instead of Twitter after the deal, per TechCrunch.

exit.reason: Terms not officially disclosed; TechCrunch reported a price slightly below 10 million dollars. The AdWords product was shut down by June 30, 2011 and the team joined Twitter revenue engineering.

competitors.name: Clickable
competitors.what: Search engine marketing and keyword bidding management

technical_complexity.rationale: Automating keyword selection and bidding through the AdWords API plus a browser toolbar needed real data work but was within reach of a small team.

defensibility.rationale: The product depended on Google AdWords data and APIs, and many SEM tools existed; nothing structural stopped competitors.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Twitter bought the team in May 2011 for its ad skills and shut down the AdWords product.

market_need_then: AdWords was a large and growing channel and small businesses lacked expertise; the founder pitched the company as the TurboTax of search engine marketing.

branding.domain_note: Not found; the YC listing shows no website.
branding.brand_signature: GrokBar, a browser toolbar showing AdWords data on a company's pages

brand_strength.rationale: Trade press launch coverage but little brand coverage; the name came from the Grok word in 1961 fiction, but no source ties AdGrok to it, so origin stays unknown.

outcome_analysis: AdGrok launched in August 2010, raised 470 thousand dollars of angel money in March 2011 and sold to Twitter in May 2011 for a reported price just under 10 million dollars, with the team joining Twitter revenue engineering and the AdWords service shut down by June 30. It was effectively an acquihire built on Google AdWords, and the CEO went to Facebook instead of Twitter.
notes: The 470K round is described as angel funding and is recorded as other. The sub-10M price is a TechCrunch report and not an official figure so amount_usd is null. No company website was recorded in the directory and none was fetched. The first competitor search found only Clickable. Founder education and prior employers not found.
